0.title: Tutorial
0.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when IN1 is off and IN2 is on.

1.title: NOT
1.desc: Invert IN1 and send it to OUT1.

2.title: OR
2.desc: Turn OUT1 on when either IN1 or IN2 is 1.

3.title: AND
3.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when IN1 and IN2 are both 1.

4.title: NOR
4.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when IN1 and IN2 are both 0.

5.title: NAND
5.desc: Turn OUT1 on when either IN1 or IN2 is 0.

6.title: XOR
6.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when IN1 and IN2 differ.

7.title: Majority
7.desc: Turn OUT1 on when at least two of IN1, IN2 and IN3 are 1.

8.title: Parity
8.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when an odd number of IN1, IN2 and IN3 are 1.

9.title: Half Adder
9.desc: Add IN1 and IN2 and output OUT2 OUT1.
rules: COUT is the carry out (twos bit); SUM is the ones bit of the sum.

10.title: Full Adder
10.desc: Add IN1, IN2 and IN3 and output OUT2 OUT1.
rules: CIN is the carry in; COUT is the carry out (twos bit); SUM is the ones bit. The sum is 0–3.

11.title: 2-to-4 Decoder
11.desc: Turn on only the output selected by IN1 and IN2.

12.title: 4-to-1 MUX
12.desc: Send the input selected by S1 S0 to OUT1.

13.title: 2-bit Comparator
13.desc: Compare A and B and turn on only the matching output: A>B, A=B or A<B.
rules: A1 A0 and B1 B0: 0–3 each.

14.title: 2-bit Adder
14.desc: Output A+B as S2 S1 S0.
rules: A1 A0 and B1 B0: 0–3 each. Output the full sum, 0–6, including carry.

15.title: 2-bit Subtractor
rules: A1 A0 and B1 B0: 0–3 each. Add 4 to a negative result.

16.title: Max Selector
16.desc: Output the larger of A and B as M1 M0.
rules: A1 A0 and B1 B0: 0–3 each. If equal, output that value.

17.title: 2-bit Multiplier
17.desc: Output A×B as P3 P2 P1 P0.
rules: A1 A0 and B1 B0: 0–3 each. The product is 0–9.

18.title: Remainder
18.desc: Output the remainder of A divided by 3 as R1 R0.
rules: A3 A2 A1 A0: 0–15. The remainder is 0, 1 or 2.

19.title: Crossroad
19.desc: Pass IN1 to OUT1 and IN2 to OUT2 unchanged.

20.title: Fixed XOR
20.desc: Turn OUT1 on only when IN1 and IN2 differ.

21.title: Rotator
21.desc: Use IN4 to select the output positions of three signals.
rules: Respond immediately to input changes; do not rotate repeatedly on ticks.

22.title: Fixed 2-to-4 Decoder
22.desc: Turn on only the output selected by IN1 and IN2.

23.title: Priority Selector
23.desc: Turn on only the output for the highest-priority input that is 1.
rules: IN1 > IN2 > IN3 > IN4. Each input selects the OUT with the same number.

24.title: 2’s Complement
24.desc: Find C so the lowest four bits of A+C are 0000.
rules: A3 A2 A1 A0 and C3 C2 C1 C0: 0–15.

25.title: Register
25.desc: Store DATA on ticks with LOAD=1 and output it at VALUE.

26.title: Toggle
26.desc: Toggle LIGHT on every tick with PRESS=1.
rules: PRESS=0 retains LIGHT. Consecutive requests toggle it every tick.

27.title: 2-to-1 MUX
27.desc: Pass A to OUT when SEL=0, or B when SEL=1.

28.title: Fault Register
28.desc: Set ALARM on ticks with FAULT=1; clear it with ACK.
rules: FAULT takes priority over ACK. Both 0 retains ALARM.

29.title: Response Check
29.desc: Set GO on the tick when responses from both A and B have arrived.
rules: Remember A=1 and B=1 separately. Repeated responses from one side count once.
Once both arrive, set GO=1 and clear both records. Otherwise GO=0.
Simultaneous responses count. Both on every tick keeps GO=1.

30.title: Pulse Extender
30.desc: Keep DOOR on for three ticks starting with a tick where OPEN=1.
rules: Include the request tick. A new OPEN restarts the three ticks from that tick.
Stay 1 through two ticks after the last request; become 0 on the following tick.

31.title: Rising Edge Detector
31.desc: Set RISE when SIGNAL changes from 0 at the previous tick to 1 at the current tick.
rules: Compare only values sampled at ticks. Otherwise RISE=0.

32.title: Up/Down Counter
32.desc: Count from 0 to 3 with INC and DEC; output BIT1 BIT0.
rules: INC alone adds 1; DEC alone subtracts 1. Equal inputs retain the value.

33.title: PWM
33.desc: Cycle through four positions; turn LIGHT on in the first LEVEL positions.
rules: Start at the first position. Advance on each tick, wrapping after the fourth.
LEVEL1 LEVEL0=0–3. Changes apply immediately to the current position without moving it.
LIGHT=0, but the position keeps advancing.

34.title: Delay Timer
34.desc: Store TIME on a tick with START=1; set DONE when that delay elapses.
rules: TIME1 TIME0=0–3. Count from the tick after START; TIME=0 completes on START.
New START takes priority over completion. Ignore TIME changes while waiting.
DONE=1 only on completion ticks. Consecutive START with TIME=0 keeps it 1.

35.title: Debouncer
35.desc: After RAW has the same value for three ticks, set CLEAN to it on the third tick.
rules: Apply the rule to both 0 and 1. Retain CLEAN until then.

36.title: Round-Robin Arbiter
36.desc: Grant the requesting side access; if both request, choose the opposite of the last user.
rules: REQ_A→A_OK; REQ_B→B_OK. Only the selected side is 1; no requests gives both 0.
A lone request also updates the last user. No requests retains that memory.
No last user; A_OK=B_OK=0. The first simultaneous request chooses A.

37.title: ABBA Detector
37.desc: Set UNLOCKED when the last four received letters are ABBA.
rules: Receive only on ticks with SUBMIT=1. SIGNAL=1 means A; 0 means B.
SUBMIT=0 retains history. Earlier letters do not matter; once set, stay at 1.

38.title: Register Bank
38.desc: Store at the address selected by ADDR and output its value at Q1 Q0.
rules: Addresses 0 and 1 hold two bits each. On WRITE=1 ticks, store D1 D0 at the selected address.
ADDR changes apply immediately without a tick, regardless of WRITE. A write tick outputs the new value.
WRITE=0 retains both values. Input changes alone do not alter storage.

39.title: Undo Register
39.desc: SAVE stores D1 D0; UNDO returns once to the previous value.
rules: On SAVE ticks, back up Q1 Q0, store the new value, and set UNDO_AVAILABLE=1.
READY=1 means UNDO is available. Only then restore the backup to Q and set READY=0. Otherwise retain values.
SAVE takes priority over UNDO. Saving the same value also enables undo.

40.title: Mailbox
40.desc: Use SEND to store one DATA bit and TAKE to remove it.
rules: On each tick, TAKE before SEND. Ignore TAKE if empty; ignore SEND if still full.
Output the taken value at DATA_OUT. VALID=1 only for successful TAKE; ACCEPTED=1 only for successful SEND. Otherwise 0.
Without a take, retain DATA_OUT. FULL=1 if occupied after processing.
Empty; DATA_OUT, VALID, ACCEPTED and FULL=0.

41.title: Stack
41.desc: Store two DATA bits and remove the most recently pushed bit first.
rules: On each tick, POP before PUSH. Ignore POP if empty; ignore PUSH if still full.
Output the popped bit at DATA_OUT; VALID=1 only on successful POP. Otherwise retain DATA_OUT and set VALID=0.
After processing, EMPTY=1 if empty; FULL=1 if both slots are occupied.

42.title: Queue
42.desc: Store two DATA bits and remove the earliest pushed bit first.
rules: On each tick, POP before PUSH. Ignore POP if empty; ignore PUSH if still full.
Output the popped bit at DATA_OUT; VALID=1 only on successful POP. Otherwise retain DATA_OUT and set VALID=0.
After processing, EMPTY=1 if empty; FULL=1 if both slots are occupied.

43.title: Serial Receiver
43.desc: Receive DATA on ticks with RECEIVE=1; update Q when four bits have arrived.
rules: Only the fourth receive tick updates all of Q and sets DONE=1. Otherwise retain Q and set DONE=0.
Start a new group after four bits.
No bits received; Q3 Q2 Q1 Q0=0000; DONE=0.

44.title: Serial Transmitter
44.desc: When idle, START accepts D3 D2 D1 D0 to send in order at SERIAL.
rules: Send D3 on the start tick, then D2→D1→D0 on the next three ticks. Ignore START and data changes meanwhile.
VALID=1 on send ticks. BUSY=1 if more bits remain; BUSY=0 on the last bit.
Restart from the tick after the last bit. While idle, retain SERIAL; VALID=BUSY=0.
RESET takes priority, cancels transmission and clears SERIAL, VALID and BUSY to 0.

45.title: Accumulator
45.desc: On ticks with ADD=1, add D1 D0 to the sum and output Q1 Q0.
rules: Subtract 4 if the sum reaches 4 or more. ADD=0 retains the sum.
RESET=1 takes priority over ADD and clears the sum to 0.

46.title: Divider
46.desc: Divide A by B to produce quotient Q and remainder R; signal completion with COMPLETE.
rules: A2 A1 A0=0–7; B1 B0=1–3. Inputs stay fixed during calculation.
Q2 Q1 Q0 and R1 R0 must be correct at the first COMPLETE=1 on ticks 1–10.
Earlier Q and R are unrestricted. Failure to complete by tick 10 fails.
Each calculation starts with all D=0.

47.title: Capacity Check
47.desc: Set OVER only when A+B is greater than LIMIT.
rules: A1 A0, B1 B0 and L1 L0: 0–3 each. L1 L0 is LIMIT.
Compare the full sum, 0–6, without truncation. Equality gives OVER=0.

hints.content: Compare the OR output with the goal. Which inputs give a different result?
Use AND to combine “at least one is on” with “both are not on together”.
When the output is on, look for a pair of inputs that are both on.
Check each pair of the three inputs with AND, then combine those results with OR.
The XOR operation works like addition mod 2.
(A XOR B) XOR C
Determine what operations OUT1 and OUT2 perform on IN1 and IN2.
OUT1 = A XOR B, OUT2 = A∧B
Determine what operations OUT1 and OUT2 perform on IN1, IN2, and IN3.
OUT1 = (A∧B)∨(B∧C)∨(C∧A), OUT2 = (A XOR B) XOR C
Try building circuits for A∧B, A∨B, and C instead of A, B, and C.
Combine circuits for OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, and OUT4 into one.
OUT1, OUT2, OUT3, and OUT4 can be expressed as AND operations of IN1, IN2, ¬IN1, and ¬IN2.
Use ternary operations.
Process S1 and S0 sequentially.
Treat (A,B,S) as a ternary operator: ((IN1,IN2,S0),(IN3,IN4,S0),S1)
Connect DATA to D and LOAD to EN.
Feed NOT Q back into D, and enable storage with PRESS.
Enable the two paths with SEL and NOT SEL, then combine them with OR.
Store FAULT with EN=FAULT OR ACK.
Remember which paths have responded. Make sure responses used for one check cannot be reused for the next.
Remember three OPEN samples with D blocks and combine them using two binary OR gates.
Store the previous SIGNAL and the detected edge in separate D blocks. Compute the edge using the old previous value.
Remember the captured setting and the remaining time. Keep completion visible until the next tick, and discard the old timer whenever START arrives.
Remember two previous RAW samples and CLEAN. Set on three ones, clear on three zeros, otherwise hold.
Determine when each bit toggles. D enables can simplify holding the value.
Remember the four-slot cycle with two bits. Consider an order that changes only one bit at a time.
Remember the last winner with EN=request present, and register whether this tick had any request.
Shift submitted letters using SUBMIT as EN. Detect the previous A,B,B and the new A; retain the unlocked state.
Derive the toggle condition for each bit, including carry. Use enabled memories and give RESET priority.
Give each word its own write enable, then select the addressed word for reading.
Keep current and backup words plus an availability bit. SAVE must copy the old current value into the backup.
Keep received bits and a four-step progress state. Publish all four bits together and register DONE for exactly the completion tick.
Store the captured word and transmission progress. Register SERIAL and VALID, and derive BUSY from the remaining work.
Track two data slots and occupancy. Preserve the last popped value independently of the current top, and register POP success.
Track the head, tail and occupancy. A POP exposes the oldest item and shifts any remaining item toward the head. Keep the last popped value separately.
Keep payload, occupancy and last delivered data separately. Process a successful TAKE before deciding whether SEND can be accepted.
You can count units while accumulating quotient and remainder, then assert COMPLETE. The example solution finishes in A+1 ticks, but ANY correct first completion within 10 ticks is accepted.
When A=1, B=2, LIMIT=3, the total equals the limit, so OVER=0. When A=2, B=2, LIMIT=3, the actual sum is 4, so OVER=1. For A=0, B=2, LIMIT=1 gives OVER=1 while LIMIT=3 gives OVER=0.

First compare the upper-bit sum A1+B1 with L1. If it is greater, OVER=1; if it is smaller, OVER=0. Only when they are equal, check whether the lower-bit sum A0+B0 exceeds L0. Call this lower-bit result C.

Connect the following equations in order. Every AND/OR has two inputs, and C means A0+B0>L0. Use JUNCTIONs to branch B0 and C. Q is an intermediate signal name.
NL0 = NOT(L0)
G0 = AND(A0, B0)
P0 = OR(A0, B0)
H0 = AND(P0, NL0)
C = OR(G0, H0)

NL1 = NOT(L1)
G1 = AND(A1, B1)
P1 = OR(A1, B1)
Q = OR(NL1, C)
T = AND(NL1, C)
U = AND(P1, Q)
V = OR(G1, T)
W = OR(V, U)
OVER <- W
